subject: Exec authority request: one-time rebate for postponed API feature
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Exec authority request: one-time rebate for postponed API feature

Team —

Quick background: Evergreen Health (pilot customer, EVG-4382) is scheduled to go live with a billing-committed pilot next month. Their implementation depends on the new multi-model routing API (route-by-model) that was in our Q3 roadmap but slipped due to a kernel integration issue. They’ve paused their final sign-off and are asking for a commercial accommodation while we finish the feature.

Customer ask (summary):
- One-time credit to offset launch impact while we complete route-by-model (they estimate 6–8 weeks delay).
- Commitment: stay on current pricing if feature lands within 8 weeks.

Attached is a short proposal I drafted (rate_makeup_proposal.pdf) and the pilot usage report the customer sent (evergreen_pilot_report.csv). I need an exec-level sign-off to approve up to a $30k one-time credit or a 15% make-good over three billing cycles — whichever you prefer.

Please review and advise:
1) Product: confirm the ETA and whether a partial mitigation (routing fallback) is realistic to reduce the commercial ask.
2) RevOps/Finance: what guardrails do we need (SOW amendment, clawback language, duration)?
3) Sales: are we comfortable with the ask vs. churn risk?

We need a decision by EOD Wed (they pushed for a commitment to keep their renewal motion on track).

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: rate_makeup_proposal.pdf
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec authority request: one-time rebate for postponed API feature

Laura —

Thanks for the write-up. Heard directly from Alyssa this morning: they’ve already built a significant portion of their integration against our existing single-model endpoint and were planning to switch to route-by-model for the 3rd party model mix with higher throughput. The pause is causing their internal compliance team to delay production.

Customer sentiment: high willingness to stay if we provide a temporary offset; their procurement wants a clear end-date and assurance no further rate increases in the next quarter.

Commercial ask (concrete terms they proposed):
- Option A: $45,000 one-time credit applied to the next invoice (their preference).
- Option B: 15% monthly credit for three months (equivalent to ~ $32k).

My read: approving something smaller and tying it to a definitive product ETA + SOW amendment is safest. If Product can commit to an 8-week delivery, we can offer Option B with a cap at $30k.

I attached the customer pilot export they sent (evergreen_pilot_report.csv).

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Rachel.Kim@redwoodinference.com

Folks —

Thanks for flagging. Quick technical notes: the route-by-model capability hit a regressions window when we rolled the new KV-cache kernel; the fix is authored and in validation. Current conservative ETA: 5–7 business weeks for full rollout to hosted customers (we can speed a specific account path with an engineering hotfix and targeted canary).

Mitigation options I can commit to:
- Engineering hotfix + focused rollout to Evergreen within ~3 weeks (risks: higher QA overhead; needs SRE support).
- Temporary routing shim that preserves their current expected call pattern (no new API surface) — deployable in ~2 weeks but it’s brittle and requires a short-term support SLA.

Recommendation: offer the smaller commercial accommodation (cap at $30k or 15% for three cycles) AND commit to the hotfix path with 3-week targeted rollout. If RevOps wants stronger clawback language, we can include rollback if feature misses the 6-week mark.

I’ll sync with SRE if we decide to pursue the hotfix option.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Management | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

> On Sep 13, 2026, at 9:21 AM, Rachel Kim wrote:
> > Customer would accept Option B if tied to ETA.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec authority request: one-time rebate for postponed API feature

Laura/Rachel/Karthik —

From a RevOps/finance control perspective:
- We can process a one-time credit up to $30k without CFO escalation if the contract amendment is signed and we have an explicit acceptance milestone.
- For recurring credits (e.g., 15% for 3 months) we need a signed amendment and a ticket in our billing system that ties the credit schedule to the new delivery date.
- Required docs: amended SOW, executive approval email for audit trail, and a HubSpot note referencing the amendment. I attached an amendment template (amendment_template.docx) we typically use.

If product can commit to the hotfix path (3-week targeted rollout) I recommend:
1) Approve Option B (15% for 3 months) capped at $30k.
2) Condition: amendment signed before the next invoice date, and the ticket created in billing.

I’ll prep the amendment once we have exec sign-off and the deal ID (EVG-4382) confirmed in HubSpot.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

The alternative (customer-preferred) is a $45k one-time credit, which is outside my delegated authority.

Why this matters: Evergreen is a strategic pilot in health care vertical; losing momentum now puts the full enterprise roll-out (Q1) at risk. We have a clear mitigation path and a concrete acceptance milestone.

Doc highlights: rate_makeup_proposal.pdf (summary and proposed language), evergreen_pilot_report.csv (customer usage), amendment_template.docx (RevOps template).
